Note::to_utf8_lossy¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::to_utf8_lossy() const

Promote Bytes To Text, Replacing Anything Not Valid UTF-8¶

to_utf8_lossy() converts a bytes-mode Note to UTF-8 text, walking each cell as UTF-8 and substituting the Unicode replacement character � (U+FFFD) for every byte or partial sequence that is not well-formed. Unlike to_utf8_strict it never raises — reach for it when you would rather carry on with a marked-up best effort than fail on a malformed payload (log lines, scraped text, mixed-encoding dumps).

Well-formed sequences are copied through byte-for-byte; only the invalid spans are rewritten, and each maladjusted byte contributes one � (so \xFF\x80 becomes two replacement characters). A cell that is already valid UTF-8 is unchanged apart from the encoding tag. The operation is shape-preserving and cell-independent.

Because it consumes anything, to_utf8_lossy() is also the front half of to_latin1_lossy and to_windows1252_lossy: they normalize to clean UTF-8 with this routine before encoding down to the single-byte target.

Example 1: Invalid Bytes Become The Replacement Character¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::bytes({std::string("ok-") + '\xFF' + "-" + '\x80' + "-end"})
        .to_utf8_lossy())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["ok-�-�-end"]

\xFF and \x80 are each replaced by one � (U+FFFD); the ASCII around them is untouched.

Example 2: Valid UTF-8 Is Unchanged¶

std::cout << pluss::note::bytes({"café"}).to_utf8_lossy() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["café"]

See Also¶

  • Note::to_utf8_strict: raise instead of substituting.

  • Note::from_latin1 / Note::from_windows1252: reinterpret the bytes in a legacy encoding rather than replacing them.
